# probe-rs writes it to 0x8000 when given `--idf-partition-table
# partitions.csv` (the cargo runner in .cargo/config.toml passes it); without
# that flag probe-rs writes its stock table
# `tracks`. The firmware reads the table back at boot (src/storage.rs) and
# finds its partitions by label
column2: so no offsets are repeated in code.

column1: # A flash writes only the bootloader
column2: this table and the app image

column1: # erases only what they cover: everything below 0x10000 plus the app image
# rounded up to whole erase blocks. The image is limited to `factory`
# (probe-rs refuses a bigger one)
# boundary where `factory` ends
column2: so no erase ever reaches it: settings and

column1: # tracks survive reflashing. (The stock `nvs` at 0x9000 does not -- it is
# inside the bootloader's erase -- which is why nothing of ours lives there.)
# settings  key/value map (sequential-storage): WiFi credentials.
#           Written by the `provision` binary
# tracks    reserved for GPS traces; unused so far (see src/storage.rs).
#           Subtype `undefined` (0x06)
#           data: a numeric data subtype such as 0x40 is not accepted --
#           probe-rs's partition parser (esp-idf-part 0.6) panics on it.

nvs
phy_init
factory
settings
tracks
